title: Risk-anchored security gating and SLA elasticity engine
creator: Priya Suresh
description: Design and deliver an automated intake and prioritization engine that scores inbound security & compliance asks using explicit risk anchors (data sensitivity, regulatory scope, account revenue/tier, model/hosting sensitivity) and translates the score into an SLA elasticity decision, a remediation plan, and a fallback routing policy. The goal is to reduce manual legal/security routing, surface consistent, auditable decisions, and enable predictable SLAs for enterprise customers while preserving a fast self-serve path for low-risk asks.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake schema that captures required risk anchors (data types, jurisdiction, requested artifact, hosting constraints, account tier) and validation rules exists in Confluence
A2: Scoring algorithm spec (weights, thresholds, elasticity bands) reviewed and approved by Security, Legal, and PM
A3: Automated decision outputs (SLA band, remediation checklist, fallback policy) produced for >=90% of test cases in the evaluation harness
A4: UI/UX mocks for the intake form + triage dashboard created in Figma and validated by Solutions Engineering
A5: Webhook integration prototype with Zendesk and Redwood Console routing implemented and a demo runbook documented
A6: Rollout plan with canary to 5 pilot accounts and rollback criteria documented
A7: Security and legal sign-off recorded and evidence bundled in the ticket before production release
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff with Security, Legal, Solutions Eng. Agreed on primary risk anchors and initial weight hypotheses (data sensitivity = 40%, jurisdiction = 25%, hosting constraint = 20%, account tier = 15%).

2025-02-14: PM-led workshop to map elasticity bands to concrete SLA windows (fast/self-serve, standard 5bd, enterprise 10bd) and fallback actions (alternative hosting, model variant, engineering exception).

2025-02-18: UX deep-dive with Design. Decided to add a progressive disclosure flow to avoid friction for low-risk asks. Figma frames 01-04 created: intake-compact / intake-detailed / triage-result / evidence-suggester.
2025-02-20: Security requested adding explicit processing activity and sub-processor fields to intake schema. Updated Confluence spec and rerouted to Legal for data residency check.

2025-02-24: Engineering spike complete: prototype scoring service (stateless function + rules table) returns SLA band in <40ms for synthetic load. Github PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/triage-engine/pull/72
2025-02-25: Blocker noted: Legal wants canonical DPA clause mappings before automated exemption suggestions can be surfaced. Added dependency to legal doc work and flagged release gating.
